Computing the first derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3\left(\frac{{x}^{8}}{4}+x-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\right)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3\left(\frac{{x}^{8}}{4}+x-4{x}^{-1/2}\right)) \\  & =3\left(8\cdot \frac{{x}^{7}}{4}+1-(-\frac{1}{2})\cdot 4{x}^{-3/2}\right) \\  & =3\left(2{x}^{7}+1+2{x}^{-3/2}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3\left(2{x}^{7}+1+2{x}^{-3/2}\right)) \\  & =3\left(7\cdot 2{x}^{6}+0+(-\frac{3}{2})\cdot 2{x}^{-5/2}\right) \\  & =3\left(14{x}^{6}-3{x}^{-5/2}\right) \\  & =3\left(14{x}^{6}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{{x}^{5}}}\right).\end{aligned}
$$
